Street closures announced for 2026 Autumn Glory events in Oakland, Maryland
The Garrett County Sheriff's Office has released details about downtown street closures for this year's Autumn Glory events in Oakland. Closures affect several main streets from Thursday through Sunday due to parades and festivals. Maps of detours were referenced but not provided.
The Garrett County Sheriff's Office announced on Oct. 7 a schedule of street closures in downtown Oakland, Maryland, for the upcoming 2026 Autumn Glory festivities.
Thursday, Oct. 8 will see the Fireman's Parade with usual parade route closures beginning at 5 PM and lasting until after the event concludes. On Friday, Oct. 9 during Fall Fest, Second Street between Alder and Liberty will be closed from 9 AM to 4 PM. Green Street will close at 9 AM Friday and remain closed through Sunday afternoon.
Saturday, Oct. 10 is set for the Autumn Glory Parade with parade route closures starting at 9 AM and remaining in effect until after the parade finishes; the parade begins at 1 PM. On Sunday, Oct. 11 during the Mountain Top Cruisers Car Show, Second Street from Alder to Center, Alder Street between Second and Third, Liberty Street between First and Second, and Green Street between Second and Third will all be closed from 8 AM to 2 PM.
Maps showing each day's specific street closures are referenced but were not available at press time. Detour routes are indicated in green on parade days, according to organizers.
The Garrett County Sheriff's Office serves as a law enforcement agency dedicated to community security and crime prevention across Garrett County—including Oakland—by addressing offenses such as trespassing and drug possession while encouraging public involvement in crime prevention efforts. It also gathers tips on criminal activities or suspicious behavior through public collaboration by offering rewards for information leading to arrests. Its services include arrests, traffic stops, K-9 unit deployments, and incident investigations—and it operates throughout areas like Oakland and Garrett Highway in Maryland—all according to the official website.
